role: The concrete attribute instance: keeps the base value, modifier sets keyed by operation, name and UUID, and lazily recomputes the cached value from base plus the three operation classes.

members.name: attributeMap
members.note: back-pointer to the owning map; a native attr_instance is an array element of attr_map, no per-instance pointer

members.name: genericAttribute
members.note: the enum field which identifies the attribute

members.name: mapByOperation
members.note: one flat mods array; computeValue filters by operation instead; not a gap (triage 2026-09-25)

members.name: mapByUUID
members.note: its HashMap bucket order is emulated only when writing NBT (attr_mod_bucket); not a gap (triage 2026-09-25)

members.name: ModifiableAttributeInstance
members.note: seeds base and cache from the default and marks needs_update

members.name: getModifiersByOperation
members.note: no standalone getter; attrs_compute walks the flat list filtering each operation

members.name: func_111122_c
members.note: the flat mods array; no union of three operation sets

members.name: getModifier
members.note: UUID comparison exists only inside apply/remove

members.name: flagForUpdate
members.note: native sets needs_update inline; the watchable-set registration half has no counterpart; not a gap (triage 2026-09-25)

members.name: computeValue
members.note: operation 0 adds, 1 adds base * amount, 2 multiplies by 1 + amount, then clamps; matches living.c:147's comment

notes: Verified computeValue's operation math against attrs_compute (living.c:149) line by line. The ATTR_MAX_MODS=8 cap is a native limit with no Java analogue; Java grows its sets unboundedly. I did not verify whether any recorded entity ever holds more than 8 modifiers on one attribute. Not gaps (triage 2026-09-25, out/plan/remaining-2026-09-25.md): data structure or helper replaced by fixed arrays or inlined arithmetic (GPU contract), behavior covered by its callers. Formerly listed as missing: the three modifier maps (by operation, by name, by UUID) do not exist natively; a flat capped array replaces them and only the NBT write emulates the HashMap bucket order. flagForUpdate's registration in the map's watchable instance set has no native counterpart: no client attribute sync exists. getModifier as a public by-UUID lookup has no direct native counterpart.
